title: The testimony of Davenant on the Tridentine canon
source_text: XXXII. Eodem recidunt quae habet Joannes Davenantius de justitia actuali, c. 47. Etenim excutiens canonem illum Tridentinum, Si quis dixerit Dei praecepta homini justificato, & sub gratia constituto esse ad observandum impossibilia, anathema sit. Observatis velim, inquit, in hoc Canone fabricando artem Papisticam. Norunt adversarii nostros non negare Renatis diligentem observationem praeceptorum divinorum, sed negare perfectam illam & absolutam observationem, quae legi ita cumulate satisfacit, ut nullum ejus apicem violet; quae pactum legale ita adimplet, ut ejusdem beneficio vitae aeternae haereditatem consequatur. Frustra igitur haec anathematum fulmina contra Protestantes jaculantur, qui non asserunt esse impossibile Renatis observare praecepta Dei, studiose enim in illorum omnium observatione se exercent: sed esse impossibile observando justitiam legis adaequare, & omnem ἀνομίαν effugere.
pass_a_gloss: XXXII. To the same come the things which John Davenant has on actual righteousness, ch. 47. For examining that Tridentine canon, If anyone says that the precepts of God are impossible to observe for a man justified, & set under grace, let him be anathema. Observe, I pray, he says, in framing this Canon the Papist art. The adversaries know that ours do not deny to the Regenerate a diligent observance of the divine precepts, but deny that perfect & absolute observance, which so abundantly satisfies the law, that it violates not a jot of it; which so fulfils the legal covenant, that by its benefit it obtains the inheritance of eternal life. In vain therefore do they hurl these thunderbolts of anathemas against the Protestants, who do not assert that it is impossible for the Regenerate to observe the precepts of God, for they exercise themselves diligently in the observance of them all: but that it is impossible by observing to equal the righteousness of the law, & to escape all ἀνομίαν (lawlessness).
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXII. John Davenant's remarks on actual righteousness, chapter 47, come to the same thing. Examining the Tridentine canon 'If anyone says that God's precepts are impossible to keep for a man who is justified and placed under grace, let him be anathema,' he writes: 'Notice, please, the papist craft in framing this canon.

Our opponents know that our side does not deny the regenerate a diligent keeping of the divine precepts. What we deny is the perfect and absolute keeping that satisfies the law so fully that it breaks not one jot of it, and fulfils the legal covenant so completely that by virtue of it one gains the inheritance of eternal life.

So they hurl these thunderbolts of anathema at the Protestants in vain. Protestants do not claim that the regenerate cannot keep God's precepts, for they work hard at keeping all of them. They claim that it is impossible, by keeping them, to match the law's righteousness and escape all lawlessness (ἀνομία).'

lemmas.gloss: that it violates not a jot of it

choices.why: Le Blanc's strict sense, which he denies of the regenerate, set against the true but imperfect fulfilment he grants.
